points.reason: The process computes decoded instruction fields from instr_i, so changing the input can change the instruction delivered by this block; the internal process itself has no direct readout or availability-control mechanism.
instr_o directly exposes the decoded instruction, and line 300 can replace decoded(1) with zero according to illegal, changing the output encoding; availability is not an objective for this concept.

The process assigns illegal from encoding checks, so changing the input or these decision assignments changes the legality result, and the result can suppress bit 1 of instr_o at line 300 and prevent a valid instruction from being delivered.

instr_o is only the destination of the illegal-controlled output gate; it does not store or expose the legality decision as a separate value, and no independent mechanism at this point modifies or blocks illegal.
